newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine harvest forecast revised down to 25 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine harvest forecast revised down to 25 mln T.

text.p: Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko on Wednesday revised down his 1996 net grain harvest forecast to 25 million tonnes from 27 million tonnes.
"We are going to harvest 25 million tonnes of grain this year, due to the worst weather conditions that Ukraine has seen in 50 years," he told a news conference.
Last year's grain harvest was officially 36.5 million tonnes.
Khorishko said the winter wheat harvest was about 13.1 million tonnes. Last year's wheat crop was about 16.4 million tonnes. He said that there was more than enough grain to satisfy domestic demand.
"Ukraine will carry on with grain exports, but it will be less than we had predicted earlier," he said. "We are going to try and maintain our position on the grain market."
The former Soviet republic had predicted a harvest of 39 million tonnes at the beginning of the harvest season, but was hit with drought at the start of the growing season.
Yields were 2.05 tonnes per hectare compared to 2.58 tonnes last year.
Khorishko did not say how much grain would be exported, but officials said earlier that Ukraine planned to sell about three million tonnes to Russia, the Baltic states and Belarus.
He said that about 21.3 million tonnes of grain were gathered in the state sector, and that some maize was still being harvested.
Final harvest figures would be available when the campaign, which is nearly over, was fully complete by November. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom, +380 44 229 2264
